- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.4) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤0.2) — increase forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts in high-sentiment periods; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment >0.7 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 previous days’ values.
